results.conclusion: The reserve documentation lists Mainnet settings of 1 XRP per account and 0.2 XRP per owned item at access time, and warns that other networks can differ. An XRPL wallet needs a base reserve plus applicable owner reserves, separately from the money it intends to send. Base reserve supports the account's existence; owner reserve constrains ledger objects. Removing an object can release its reserve requirement. Reserves are not payments to validators, and the documentation permits reserved XRP to pay transaction costs. Treating every XRP in a balance as transferable would therefore confuse several distinct accounting concepts. A wallet with enough principal for a purchase may still lack room for the escrow object or transaction fee.
